title: A birational model with an invariant boundary divisor
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], where separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Integral means reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme]; normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth integral $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with identity $e$. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $X_0$ be normal integral and proper, and let $Y\subseteq X_0$ be a smooth dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] with a regular $G$-action. Assume $E_0=X_0\setminus Y$ is nonempty and every irreducible component has codimension one. A rational map means an equivalence class of morphisms on dense open subschemes, taken on its largest open domain of definition. Let $\alpha_0:G\times_kX_0\dashrightarrow X_0$ be the rational extension of this action. There exist a normal integral proper $k$-scheme $X$, a proper birational morphism $b:X\to X_0$ that is an isomorphism over $Y$, and an integral closed subscheme $D\subseteq X\setminus Y$ of dimension $\dim X_0-1$. Here birational means inducing an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. Identify $Y$ with $b^{-1}(Y)$ and let $\alpha:G\times_kX\dashrightarrow X$ be the rational extension of its action, with domain $U$. The intersection $U_D=U\cap(G\times_kD)$ is dense open in $G\times_kD$, and $\alpha|_{U_D}$ factors through $D$. The rational map $\tau:G\times_kD\dashrightarrow G\times_kD$, $(g,x)\mapsto(g^{-1},\alpha(g,x))$, is a birational involution. More precisely, there is a nonempty open $W\subseteq U_D$ on which $\tau$ is an isomorphism $W\to W$ and satisfies $\tau^2=\mathrm{id}_W$. Also $\dim X=\dim X_0$.

proof.text: Put $n=\dim X_0$. We will use the following dimension calculation on integral finite-type $k$-schemes $Q$. Every nonempty open has dimension $\dim Q$ by [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension]; hence $\dim_qQ=\dim Q$ by [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. For an integral closed subset $C$ with generic point $c$, [lem-kun-dimension-formula] and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] give $\dim\mathcal O_{Q,c}=\dim Q-\dim C$. In particular a prime divisor has dimension $\dim Q-1$. All schemes of finite type over $k$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The interpretation of codimension as this local-ring dimension is [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains].

proof.text: The dimension convention in [lem-sfb-scheme-product-dimension] agrees with topological dimension by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings]. For any normal integral $k$-variety $Q$, [lem-sfb-algclosed-integral-product] makes $G\times_kQ$ integral. Its projection to $Q$ is smooth: $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], so [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] applies to the smooth, locally finitely presented structure map of $G$. Thus [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] makes the product normal. At each codimension-one point its local ring is a DVR by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr], hence a valuation ring by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. For a proper target, [lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point] therefore puts every such point in the maximal rational-map domain. Apply this to $Q=X_0$ and $\alpha_0$. Choose a reduced boundary component $E_1$. Step 1 and [lem-sfb-scheme-product-dimension] show that $G\times_kE_1$ has codimension one in $G\times_kX_0$. Consequently $T=\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha_0)\cap(G\times_kE_1)$ is a nonempty dense open of this integral divisor, and a prime divisor in the normal integral source $V=\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha_0)$.

proof.text: The map $\alpha_0:V\to X_0$ is dominant since its restriction to $G\times_kY$ is the action and contains $Y$ in its image. Its defined boundary points map into $E_0$: if $g\cdot z\in Y(k)$ for $z\notin Y(k)$, then $g^{-1}\cdot(g\cdot z)$ is defined in $Y$, while [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws] makes it equal to $z$, a contradiction. Closed points are dense and $k$-rational by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so the inverse image of the closed set $E_0$ contains all of $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-prime-divisor-image-extraction] to $(V,X_0,\alpha_0,T,E_0)$. Obtain $b:X\to X_0$, an isomorphism over $Y$, normal integral proper $X$, and the integral divisor $D\subset b^{-1}(E_0)$ of dimension $n-1$ which is the closure of the lifted image of $T$. Since $b$ is an isomorphism over the nonempty open $Y$, [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] gives $\dim X=\dim Y=\dim X_0=n$ already at this stage.

proof.text: Let $E_1^{\prime}$ be the strict transform of $E_1$ in $X$, namely the reduced closure of its inverse image on an isomorphism open of $b$ containing its generic point. Such an open exists by [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one], since the generic local ring of $E_1$ in normal $X_0$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. The isomorphism on these dense opens identifies $G\times E_1^{\prime}$ birationally with $G\times E_1$. Let $\alpha:G\times X\dashrightarrow X$ extend the action on $Y$, as in [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws]. Its rational identity $\alpha=b^{-1}\alpha_0(1\times b)$ follows by checking on $G\times Y$. Thus on a dense open $R\subset G\times E_1^{\prime}$ its restriction is a dominant morphism $r:R\to D$, by the image-closure assertion of the extraction lemma. The open $U_D=\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha)\cap(G\times D)$ is dense in integral $G\times D$: step 2 applies to normal $X$, since $D$ has codimension one by step 1.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational-action paragraph, referring to Milne (2013), arXiv:1311.6060v2, Proposition 4.1 proof and Lemmas 4.3--4.4, pp.8--9 (read online; local article WANTED).

proof.text: The rational map $\lambda:G\times G\times E_1^{\prime}\dashrightarrow G\times D$, $(g,h,z)\mapsto(g,r(h,z))$, is dominant. Indeed $r$ has scheme-theoretic image $D$ by [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], and its base change along the flat projection $G\times D\to D$ has the same property by [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback]; flatness follows from the smooth projection of step 2 and [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. On a dense open of the triple product, both $g\cdot(h\cdot z)$ and $(gh)\cdot z$ are defined: use dominance of $\lambda$ for the first and the automorphism $(g,h,z)\mapsto(g,gh,z)$ for the second. The domain laws give $g\cdot(h\cdot z)=(gh)\cdot z\in D$ on its $k$-points. These are dense by the two closed-point lemmas. Since the image of this dense open under $\lambda$ is dense in $G\times D$, the closed inverse image of $D$ under $\alpha|_{U_D}$ is all of $U_D$. The source is reduced by [lem-sfb-algclosed-integral-product], so [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] gives the required scheme-theoretic factorization through $D$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational-action paragraph, referring to Milne (2013), arXiv:1311.6060v2, Proposition 4.1 proof and Lemmas 4.3--4.4, pp.8--9 (read online; local article WANTED).

proof.text: Now $\tau(g,x)=(g^{-1},g\cdot x)$ is a rational self-map of integral $G\times D$. It is dominant, a point not supplied by its formula alone: on the dense triple-product open of step 5, $\tau\lambda(g,h,z)=(g^{-1},r(gh,z))$. The latter is dominant, since it is $\lambda$ precomposed with the automorphism $(g,h,z)\mapsto(g^{-1},gh,z)$, whose inverse is $(a,b,z)\mapsto(a^{-1},ab,z)$. Thus $\tau$ is dominant. Its square is defined on a dense open. At its $k$-points, the composition and unit identities of [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws] give $g^{-1}\cdot(g\cdot x)=e\cdot x=x$. The closed points are dense and $k$-rational by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] to their disjoint union mapping densely into the reduced open source; this makes $\tau^2=1$ an equality of rational maps. The two coordinates agree, since inversion squared is the identity on $G$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational-action paragraph, referring to Milne (2013), arXiv:1311.6060v2, Proposition 4.1 proof and Lemmas 4.3--4.4, pp.8--9 (read online; local article WANTED).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-inverse-partial-map-restrictions] to $\tau$ and itself. It gives an isomorphism $f:A\to B$ on dense opens with $A\subset U_D$ and $f$ the restriction of $\tau$; its statement does not require $B\subset U_D$. Set $B_0=B\cap U_D$ and $A_0=f^{-1}(B_0)$. These are dense nonempty opens and $f:A_0\to B_0$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse agrees with $\tau|_{B_0}$ on a dense open, because $\tau^2=1$ as a rational map. By [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] the agreement holds everywhere on reduced $B_0$. Now set $W=A_0\cap B_0\subset U_D$. For $x\in W$, its image under $\tau$ lies in $B_0$ using $x\in A_0$, and in $A_0$ using $x\in B_0$ and the inverse description. Thus $\tau:W\to W$ is an isomorphism with square the identity. The open $W$ is nonempty by irreducibility of $G\times D$. Finally $b$ identifies nonempty opens of integral $X,X_0$, so [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] gives $\dim X=\dim X_0=n$.

Sources: Milne iAG2017 Prop 8.25 p.154; Milne 2013 (arXiv 1311.6060v2, read online) Def 4.2, Lemmas 4.3-4.4 and the Prop 4.1 proof; Stacks varieties.tex:85-141, Tag 05P3. Not a re-split: the item was new and had no earlier proof, and its statement is unchanged apart from the TeX escapes. Step 1: the dimension formula and trdeg give dim O_{Q,c} = dim Q - dim C. Step 2: the product is integral; it is normal because its projection is smooth (flat base change, with flatness from pc-flat-field); codimension-one local rings are DVRs, hence valuation rings, so the valuation-point extension puts these points in the domain. Step 3: the domain laws (with h=g, then g^{-1}, then the unit law) show the boundary maps into E_0, using Jacobson and k-rational closed points; every hypothesis of the extraction node holds. Step 4: normal-modification-codim-one (2) gives the strict transform; alpha = b^{-1} alpha_0 (1 x b), so r: R -> D is dominant. Step 5: lambda = 1 x r is dominant by reduced image plus nagata flat pullback; k-point density plus the reduced-source factorization give alpha(U_D) in D. Step 6: tau.lambda = lambda.sigma (checked sigma and its inverse), so tau is dominant; tau^2 = id via the unit and composition laws and separated extensionality. Step 7: W = A_0 n B_0 is stable, nonempty and satisfies tau^2 = id. New nodes: algclosed-integral-product is the integrality part of Stacks 05P3 and true. It is not a duplicate: sc-irreducible-product-over-field and wf-affine-product-reduced are partial, and integral-pullback-geometric-flat-open needs geometric integrality. prime-divisor-image-extraction is true: w = ord_T restricted to k(P) is nontrivial with center in Z; Abhyankar gives residue trdeg >= dim P - 1; blowups centred inside b^{-1}(Z) plus normalization (Kollar-Mori 2.45) leave P\Z unchanged; the valuative criterion at the DVR O_{V,eta_T} defines f'. Its agent-written refinement is labelled as such in the source field. It does not restate the item and is not a duplicate of the trf valuation-curve nodes or cor-nagata-conrad. Batch 5: smooth-at-point fibre criterion, def-trf-valuation-ring, affine dimension inequality and reduced scheme image are generic facts or definitions, not parts of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs, so I accept them. tool_uses accepted; no fixes.
